title: December, on the dock
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Does Chloe come home. She does. One strip. The dock. They don't talk about it.

panels.composition: Gully's dock, December dusk, the chair under the eave. CHLOE at the end of the dock — here, real, older, a city coat. WOOD arriving with BARNABY. The dog gets there first.

characters.pose: at the dock end, city coat

image.prompt: a young woman in a city coat standing at the end of a wooden dock at winter dusk, a small dog running to her, a young man in a chore coat arriving behind, brush-pen black and white
image.notes: Chloe at 21 — draw her older than the 1999 model: shorter hair, a real coat. Same eyeliner.

panels.composition: The two of them sitting. Feet over the water. The dog between.

balloons.text: Three days. My mother's sick of me already.

image.prompt: a young woman and a young man sitting at the end of a dock with a small dog between them, feet over dark water

panels.composition: Chloe, looking at the shack's new sign, hand-painted, half done: GULLY'S T—

balloons.text: I have a job and a dog.

image.prompt: a young woman looking back at a shingle shack with a half-painted hand-lettered sign, dusk

panels.composition: The three of them at the dock's end, from behind, small. Dusk. That's the whole visit. The strip gives it one strip.

image.prompt: two young people and a small dog seen from behind sitting at the end of a dock at dusk over dark water, small in the frame, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; xerox; black and white

notes: She comes home. One strip. From behind. The strip is learning restraint from the dock.
